chapters.title: Campaign and Journey Optimization
chapters.overview: Master campaign and journey optimization for Adobe Journey Optimizer certification.
chapters.fullContent:
Journey Types & Entry Points 
1. Unitary Event Journey 
Trigger: Customer performs an action (click, purchase, form submission) Timing: Real-time, immediate Reentrance: 5-minute block (default) Event payload limit: 64 KB 
Best for: Immediate reactions, real-time personalization 
Example: Customer abandons cart → email within 15 minutes 
Key guardrails: 5-minute reentrance block prevents duplicate messages 
64 KB event payload limit (exceeding drops event silently) 
1 MB journey instance limit (data accumulation during execution) 
Cannot coexist with business events in same journey 
2. Business Event Journey 
Trigger: External system sends an event (not customer action) Timing: Scheduled or batch Best for: Aggregated data, scheduled sends 
Example: Daily purchase summary email at midnight 
Key guardrails: Cannot coexist with unitary events in same journey 
Cannot coexist with audience qualification 
3. Read Audience Journey 
Trigger: Scheduled batch read of an audience Timing: Daily, weekly schedule or triggered by business event Best for: Batch campaigns, audience-wide initiatives 
Example: Every Monday 9 AM, read all VIP customers and send weekly digest 
Key guardrails: 5 concurrent instances max (organization-wide) - Stagger 5-10 minutes apart 
12-hour processing timeout 
20K profiles/sec sandbox throughput 
One audience per journey 
Cannot use with Campaign Standard activities 
4. Audience Qualification Journey 
Trigger: Customer enters or exits an audience in real-time Timing: Real-time as they qualify/disqualify Activation delay: Up to 10 minutes 
Example: Churn score changes → immediately trigger retention journey 
Journey Activities 
Activity Purpose Key Use Email Send email message Send promotional/transactional email SMS Send text message Send verification code or alert Push Send mobile push notification Send app notification In-app Display message within app Show discount banner in app Condition Branch based on rules IF loyalty_tier = VIP THEN... ELSE... chapters.title: Offer Decisioning
chapters.overview: Master offer decisioning for Adobe Journey Optimizer certification.
chapters.fullContent:
Core Concepts 
1. Offer 
An individual piece of content/promotion Examples: "Get 20% off", "Free shipping", product recommendation Contains: Name, channels, content, constraints, eligibility rules 
2. Collection 
Grouping of related offers Example: "Summer Promotions" collection with 5 summer offers Purpose: Organize offers logically, control scope 
3. Decision 
Logic that selects which offer to show Specifies: Collection, eligibility rules, ranking/priority, capping, fallback offer 
4. Placement 
Where and how offer is delivered Tied to channel: Email header, Web banner, SMS text, In-app popup 
5. Decision Policy 
Complete machine that brings it all together Formula: Decision Policy = Collection + Decision Logic + Placements + Offers 
The 4 Stages of Offer Decisioning 
Stage 1: Create Offers Define individual offers with content, channels, constraints Set eligibility rules per offer Status: Draft → Approved → Live 
Stage 2: Organize Into Collections Group related offers Creates logical structure 
Stage 3: Build Decisions Create decision logic (ranking, capping, eligibility) Select collection Define fallback offers Set up constraints 
Stage 4: Deploy Decisions Use decision in journey via Content Decision activity System evaluates rules in real-time for each customer Best matching offer selected and delivered 
Static vs. Dynamic Offers 
Aspect Static Offer Dynamic Offer Definition Fixed content for all customers Content changes based on customer data Example "Get 20% off your next purchase" "Get {{discountPercentage}}% off, {{firstName}}" Personalization None (same for everyone) Uses profile attributes, dynamic fields Complexity Simple, easy to manage More complex, needs data setup Performance Faster (no data lookup needed) Slightly slower (evaluates expressions) Exam Pattern: If scenario says "personalize based on customer data" → dynamic offer 
Capping & Ranking Logic 
How Capping Works 
Capping is PER-OFFER , not decision-level 
Example: Offer A: "Robo-Advisor Service" (priority 1, capped at 3/month) Offer B: "Managed Portfolio" (priority 2, capped at 3/month) Offer C: "Self-Directed Trading" (priority 3, capped at 3/month) Customer has received Offer A 3 times this month (capped) System evaluates: A is capped, skip it System evaluates: B hasn't reached cap → deliver B (Does NOT deliver fallback) 
Key Rule: When top-priority offer is capped → system selects next ranked uncapped offer. Does NOT fail decision.

chapters.title: Content Authoring
chapters.overview: Master content authoring for Adobe Journey Optimizer certification.
chapters.fullContent:
Personalized Fields 
What They Are 
Placeholders replaced with actual customer data at send time 
Syntax 
{{profile.attributes.firstName}}
{{event.productName}}
{{profile.segmentMembership.goldTier}}
{{context.journeyName}} 
Data Sources 
Profile attributes: firstName, email, loyaltyTier, lastPurchaseDate 
Event data: productViewed, cartValue, eventTime 
Contextual data: journeyName, campaignId 
Key Rules 
✅ Fields must exist in profile or event schema 
❌ Cannot reference non-existent fields (causes failure) 
✅ Can use conditional logic: {{if profile.attributes.loyaltyTier == "VIP" then "exclusive offer" else "standard offer"}} 
Visual Fragments 
What: Pre-designed HTML blocks (headers, footers, banners, images) Size limit: 100 KB max Channels: Email ONLY Status required: Must be "Live" to use 
Use Cases 
Include branded footer in every email 
Reuse logo + social links + unsubscribe + copyright 
Static design blocks that don't change per customer 
Benefits 
✅ Consistency across all emails 
✅ Update once, all messages update 
✅ Version control for shared content 
Expression Fragments 
What: Reusable personalization logic/expressions Size limit: 200 KB max Channels: Email, SMS, Push (NOT in-app) Status required: Must be "Live" to use 
Example 
{{if profile.attributes.loyaltyTier == "GOLD" 
 then "You get 30% off" 
 else "You get 10% off"}} 
Use Cases 
Apply same loyalty tier logic to all messages 
IF/THEN logic for different messages 
Reusable business rules 
Critical Rule 
Expression fragments CANNOT be used in in-app messages Use personalization fields for in-app instead 
Email Templates 
What: Pre-designed email structure Use: Reuse layout and branding across journeys Can include: Personalization fields, fragments, dynamic content 
Template vs. Fragment Difference 
Template Fragment Entire email structure Reusable content block Layout + content Personalization logic OR visual block Multiple uses across journeys Inserted into templates Can be modified per use Must stay consistent (live status) Asset Essentials 
What: System for storing and managing images/files Benefit: Images update automatically when source changes 
Features 
Upload images to central repository 
Reference by asset ID in emails 
Version control (update source, all references update) 
Organize in folders 
Content Experiments (A/B Testing) 
What You Can Test 
✅ Subject line variations 
✅ Email body copy variations 
✅ Call-to-action button text 
✅ Images/visual elements 
✅ Different offers

chapters.title: Foundations of Adobe Experience Platform
chapters.overview: Master foundations of adobe experience platform for Adobe Journey Optimizer certification.
chapters.fullContent:
Schemas: Profile vs. Event 
Memory Trick 
PROFILE = "WHO is the customer?" (Static attributes) EVENT = "WHAT did they do?" + "WHEN?" (Time-series actions) 
Profile Schema (XDM Individual Profile) 
Purpose: Stores customer attributes (WHO they are) Data type: Personal info — name, email, age, preferences, loyalty tier When enabled for profile: Profile data stored in Unified Profile Service (real-time access) Example fields: firstName, lastName, email, phone, loyaltyTier, lastPurchaseDate 
Event Schema (XDM ExperienceEvent) 
Purpose: Stores what customers did (behavioral events) Data type: Time-series events — purchase, click, view, search When enabled for profile: Event data stored and linked to customer profiles Example fields: eventType, timestamp, productViewed, purchaseAmount, pageURL 
Datasets 
Datasets Enabled for Profile 
✅ Data ingested into Unified Profile Service (real-time) 
✅ Available for real-time personalization in journeys 
✅ Can be referenced in journey conditions 
⚠️ Counts against engageable profile quota (costs money) 
Datasets NOT Enabled for Profile 
❌ Data stays in Data Lake only (not real-time) 
❌ Cannot be accessed instantly in journeys 
❌ Can be queried/analyzed but not for real-time personalization 
✅ Does NOT count against engageable profile quota (no cost) 
Exam Pattern 
"Marketer wants to use purchase history in journey condition. Dataset enabled for profile?" Answer: YES, must be enabled for profile 
Identities 
Authenticated Identities (Known Customers) 
Email: john@example.com 
CRM ID: CUST-12345 
Mobile AAID/IDFA: Unique mobile device ID 
Custom ID: Your proprietary customer ID 
Pseudonymous Identities (Anonymous/Unknown Visitors) 
ECID (Experience Cloud ID): Adobe's auto-generated ID for unknown browsers 
Used for: Tracking anonymous website visitors 
Gets merged: When visitor logs in, ECID + email link together 
Identity Merging 
Scenario: Day 1, 2 PM: Anonymous visitor (ECID-12345) views products, adds to cart Day 1, 3 PM: Same person logs in (email: john@example.com, CRM ID: CUST-54321) System links: ECID-12345 + email + CRM ID → same profile ALL historical data merges automatically Journey condition "if customer viewed products + added to cart in last 24 hours" System finds ALL merged data → triggers journey ✓ 
Engageable Profile Impact 
✅ Authenticated identities (email, CRM ID) = count as engageable 
✅ Pseudonymous identities (ECID) = count as engageable too 
💡 Solution: Set TTL (Time-To-Live) on pseudonymous profile
